title: Supreme Court lawyers hold silent protest over detention of colleagues
seoTitle: Delhi lawyers protest detention of colleagues

tea.why: Lawyers protested against the alleged police manhandling and detention of their colleagues during an October 10 demonstration.
tea.want: They demand an independent and impartial investigation into the police actions taken against advocates.
tea.changed: Oct 13: Supreme Court lawyers held a silent protest at Media Park to express solidarity with detained colleagues.

summary: Members of the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) and the Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association (SCAORA) held a silent protest at Media Park in Delhi on October 13. The gathering was organised to express solidarity with lawyers who were allegedly manhandled and detained by Delhi Police during a protest on October 10. That earlier protest concerned allegations of discrepancies in electoral rolls. During the October 13 event, participants observed a minute of silence and read the Preamble to the Constitution. The SCAORA has formally petitioned the Supreme Court, requesting an independent investigation into the police conduct and the identification of officers involved. The lawyers stated that the protest was intended to defend constitutional rights and the integrity of legal institutions, rather than to support any specific political party.
demands: Preservation of evidence regarding the incident
response: The Chief Justice of India intervened following the initial detentions on October 10, which led to the release of the detained lawyers, according to reports.

updates.text: Supreme Court lawyers held a silent protest at Media Park to support colleagues detained during an October 10 demonstration.
